audit_findings.title: Serial-acquisition reinvestment may be omitted while acquired-intangible amortization is added back
audit_findings.magnitude: $97.314 million of 2025 intangible amortization; $560 million of acquisition consideration over three years, averaging a computed $186.7 million annually
audit_findings.mechanism: Owner earnings is overstated if acquired-intangible amortization is added back without deducting the portion of recurring acquisition spending needed to sustain the existing earnings perimeter; the same issue also affects support for the assumed growth rates.
audit_findings.evidence: Over the last three years, the Company has completed acquisitions for aggregate cash consideration of approximately $560 million, net of cash acquired.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that acquisitions are a recurring and significant component of Patrick's strategy and reported earnings. The $97.314 million amortization add-back would equal 40.9% of the $238.2 million anchor, while average three-year acquisition spending equals 78.4% of the anchor. Not all acquisition spending is maintenance, so the required deduction is unresolved, but even a modest maintenance portion could materially reduce value. The supplied record does not conclusively reconcile whether the full amortization amount was added back.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2025 owner-earnings calculation line by line, separate acquired-intangible amortization from other depreciation, estimate maintenance acquisition spending using acquired revenue and operating-income retention by vintage, and rerun all scenarios with the supported recurring amount deducted.

audit_findings.title: Convertible-note treatment mixes a debt-funded earnings claim with gross equity dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: 7.753734 million gross shares included from 3.876867 million conversion shares plus 3.876867 million warrants; removing those gross blocks reduces the supplied denominator from 40.653641 million to a computed 32.899907 million and, before modeling net dilution, changes value per share to $87.02 bear, $102.61 base and $120.91 bull
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator includes gross conversion and warrant shares while owner earnings retains convertible interest and the principal remains a cash-settled debt claim; hedge and strike mechanics therefore are not aligned between earnings, debt treatment and shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company will satisfy any conversion by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the 1.75 % Convertible Notes to be converted and by paying or delivering, as the case may be, cash, shares of the Company’s common stock, or a combination of cash and shares of the Company’s common stock, at its election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of its conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the 1.75 % Convertible Notes being converted.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-definition inconsistency, not merely a possible future risk. Principal must be cash-settled, the note hedge offsets excess conversion value, and warrants dilute only above their approximately $85.30 strike. The valuation nevertheless includes both full 3.877 million-share blocks. The computed no-block values are a ceiling rather than the correct answer because option awards and net warrant dilution still require modeling, but they demonstrate that the error can readily change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun each scenario using net incremental shares under the cash-settlement, note-hedge and warrant formulas at each scenario value; alternatively use coherent assumed conversion, remove after-tax convertible interest from owner earnings and treat the converted principal consistently.

audit_findings.title: The normalized anchor may strip an economically recurring casualty cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.420 million filed pre-tax charge; a computed $18.63 million after tax using the filed 23.7% effective tax rate, equal to 7.8% of the $238.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding the settlement back raises normalized owner earnings; any recurring expected casualty, deductible, uninsured-loss or litigation cost should instead reduce the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recognized a legal settlement expense of $ 24.4 million, related to a motor-vehicle accident that resulted in two fatalities, within "Other expenses" in the Company's consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: The accident and settlement are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not conclusively reconcile the add-back or establish that comparable casualty losses recur. The filed charge is large enough to affect value if treated as recurring, yet using the full amount would also be unsupported because it arose from a specific fatal accident. Materiality therefore depends on an unquantified normalized expected-loss provision.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the exact settlement and tax adjustments in the anchor, compile at least ten years of casualty claims, deductibles, insurance recoveries and uninsured losses, and rerun with the supported annual expected-loss provision.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified Superfund exposure may be an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable uninsured remediation obligation would be deducted in the equity bridge; recurring investigation, monitoring or remediation payments could instead reduce normalized owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: However, any litigation is inherently uncertain, the EPA has yet to select a final remedy for the Superfund Site, and any judgment or injunctive relief entered against us or any adverse settlement could materially and adversely impact our business, results of operations, financial condition, and prospects.
audit_findings.explanation: The EPA designation and Patrick's possible responsibility are demonstrated, but no final remedy, allocation or loss estimate is supplied. The latest 10-Q reports no change and management does not currently expect a material adverse impact, while still acknowledging potentially material consequences. Without a remedy estimate, responsibility allocation and indemnity analysis, the record cannot establish either a zero value or material magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the EPA remedial investigation and feasibility-study estimates, proposed remedy, potentially responsible-party allocation, parcel-level indemnity terms, counterparty credit support, insurance coverage and any post-quarter accrual; then deduct the probable uninsured present value or rerun owner earnings for recurring costs.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition contingent consideration is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.761 million latest-quarter fair value, or a computed $0.04 per diluted share and 0.05% of $3.376 billion base equity value; $9.228 million maximum, or $0.23 per diluted share and 0.27% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Contingent consideration is a claim for acquired earnings already inside the operating perimeter and should reduce the equity bridge unless its expected payment is already charged in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with certain acquisitions, the Company is required to pay additional cash consideration to the sellers if certain financial results of the acquired businesses are achieved.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but the latest expected liability is only $1.761 million. Deducting it reduces base value from $83.04 to approximately $83.00 per share, still above the $82.84 price, and does not alter the $58.13 buy-below conclusion. Even the contractual maximum would not change the practical conclusion that the stock is near base value and above the margin-of-safety threshold, although it would erase the immaterial $0.20 base-price spread.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the June 2026 $1.761 million fair-value liability is not already reflected in owner earnings, deduct it from the bridge, and update the balance at the next filing or settlement.
